turns.text:
The documents indicate that the arrival date of the units matters because it affects the timing of the inspection period and whether the rejection notice was timely. turns.question: Did Apex give a valid force majeure notice?
turns.text:
Apex claimed that a flood, which was a Force Majeure Event under clause 8.1, caused a delay in delivering the replacement Units. Apex notified Morgan of the flood on June 2, 2026, by email, describing the event and the expected delivery of the replacement Units on June 10, 2026 [1].

According to clause 8.2 of the Services Agreement, the Affected Party must give written notice within five Business Days of becoming aware of the Force Majeure Event. Apex became aware of the flood on May 21, 2026, and gave notice on June 2, 2026, which was more than five Business Days later [1].

The notice must also describe the event, the obligations affected, the expected duration, and the steps taken to mitigate the effects. The email from Apex described the event and the expected delivery date, but it is unclear whether it included the steps taken to mitigate the effects of the flood [1].

Clause 8.2 also requires the notice to be given in accordance with clause 14 of the Services Agreement. The documents do not confirm whether the notice was sent to the correct address or in the correct format required by clause 14 [6].

Therefore, based on the information provided, it is unclear whether Apex gave a valid force majeure notice, as the documents do not confirm whether the notice was given within five Business Days or in the correct format.

turns.question: How much can Morgan claim in liquidated damages for the late delivery? Show the working.
turns.text:
The liquidated damages that Morgan can claim for the late delivery are calculated as follows:

The Delivery Date was amended to May 20, 2026 [6]. Delivery was completed on June 10, 2026 [6]. The period of delay is 21 days, which is exactly 3 weeks [6].

The weekly liquidated damages rate is 1.5% of the Total Contract Price [5]. The Total Contract Price is USD 1,240,000 [6].

The weekly amount is calculated as 1.5% of USD 1,240,000, which equals USD 18,600 [6]. For 3 weeks, the total liquidated damages are 3 × USD 18,600 = USD 55,800 [6].

The cap on liquidated damages is 10% of the Total Contract Price [1]. This is 10% of USD 1,240,000, which equals USD 124,000 [6].

The total liquidated damages of USD 55,800 are less than the cap of USD 124,000 [6]. Therefore, Morgan can claim USD 55,800 in liquidated damages.

turns.question: Which units were rejected, why, and which units replaced them?
turns.text:
The rejected units were IC450-1113 and IC450-1134. They were rejected because Unit IC450-1113 had a cracked condenser housing and Unit IC450-1134 had a refrigerant leak at a brazed joint in circuit 2 [3].

The units that replaced the rejected ones were IC450-1141 and IC450-1142. These replacement units were delivered on June 10, 2026, and passed inspection on June 11, 2026 [1].

turns.question: What case does the research memo rely on for the enforceability of the liquidated damages clause, and can we rely on it?
turns.text:
The research memo relies on the case *Larkspur Hydraulics Corp. v. Vantrell Fabrication Co.*, 284 A.3d 1176 (Del. 2022) for the enforceability of the liquidated damages clause [3].

The memo also states that the parties agreed in clause 7.3 of the Services Agreement that the liquidated damages amounts are "a reasonable pre-estimate of those losses and not a penalty" [3].

The memo does not provide any other case or legal authority for the enforceability of the liquidated damages clause.

turns.question: What delivery date did the Services Agreement originally set?
turns.text:
The Services Agreement (DEMO) originally set the Delivery Date as May 15, 2026. This is stated in clause 4.2 of the Services Agreement (DEMO), which reads: "4.2 Delivery Date. The Supplier shall deliver all Units to the Delivery Point on or before May 15, 2026." [2]

Later, this date was amended by Amendment No. 1. Clause 1.1 of Amendment No. 1 replaced clause 4.2 with a new Delivery Date of May 20, 2026. [6] This amendment was signed by both parties and took effect on May 14, 2026. [6]

Despite the amendment, the original Delivery Date in the Services Agreement (DEMO) was May 15, 2026. [2]
notes: Clause 4.2 of Services Agreement (DEMO) was deleted and replaced by clause 1.1 of Amendment No. 1 (DEMO) (signed). It says: “This Amendment takes effect on May 14, 2026, the date on which it has been signed by both Parties.”

Clause 7.1 of Services Agreement (DEMO) was deleted and replaced by clause 2.1 of Amendment No. 1 (DEMO) (signed). It says: “This Amendment takes effect on May 14, 2026, the date on which it has been signed by both Parties.”

turns.question: Is that still the date?
turns.text:
The documents indicate that May 15, 2026, is no longer the Delivery Date. According to source 1, Amendment No. 1, dated May 14, 2026, and signed by both parties, replaced the original date of May 15, 2026 in clause 4.2 of the Services Agreement with May 20, 2026. Additionally, source 2 states that the Delivery Date, as amended by Amendment No. 1, is May 20, 2026.

However, source 2 also claims that all forty (40) Units arrived at the Delivery Point on May 15, 2026, as shown by the carrier's records and confirmed by Morgan's own email of May 18, 2026. Source 5 confirms that the Units arrived on May 15, 2026, and source 3 mentions that the arrival date is May 15, 2026, based on the shipment and receiving log and Witness B's testimony.

Thus, while the amended Delivery Date is May 20, 2026, the actual arrival of the Units is stated to have occurred on May 15, 2026, according to multiple sources.

turns.question: When did Apex dispatch the units?
turns.text:
The documents state that Apex dispatched the units on May 10, 2026, as indicated by the email from Priya Raman, Program Manager at Apex Industries, Inc., which provided the planned dispatch date of May 10, 2026 [6].

Additionally, the dispatch notice mentioned in the Services Agreement requires that the Supplier notify the Buyer's Project Contact at least three Business Days before dispatch [5]. The email sent on May 4, 2026, which provided the planned dispatch date, supports this timeline.

turns.question: And when did they arrive?
turns.text:
The units arrived on May 12, 2026, according to Mr. Pell's testimony [1].

However, Apex states that all forty (40) units arrived at the Delivery Point on May 15, 2026 at 07:40 [2].

Additionally, the draft meeting notes mention that the units arrived on or about May 15 [3].
